pages.text: Natural uranium is 0.72% uranium-235. A reactor needs a few per cent. Roast $(item)Raw Pitchblende$() into $(item)Yellowcake$(), combine it with $(item)Fluorspar$() (the Spectrograph finds it in calcite and in geode shells) and you have $(fluid)Uranium Hexafluoride$(), a gas.

In a centrifuge spinning at hundreds of metres a second, the heavier U-238 crowds to the wall: the separation factor is α = e^(Δm v²/2RT). One stage barely helps. The $(item)Gas Centrifuge Cascade$() is a tower, one layer per stage: build the stage layer once, or stack it up to fourteen high, and every stage multiplies the ratio again.

The $(thing)cut$() is the share of each stage's feed passed upward: small cuts enrich more, large ones run faster. Spin the rotors faster for more separation, but carbon fibre bursts above about 1,500 MPa, and there is a flexural resonance near 450 m/s. Enrichment stops at 20%: reactor fuel, never more.
